correctness.rationale: An unrestricted unique minimum exists by strict inverse-trace convexity and edge-Laplacian injectivity. Symmetry then forces two conductance classes. The complete unsigned-incidence spectral decomposition includes one nontrivial constant-mode eigenvalue, n-1 coupled pairs and m-n uncoupled 2y modes; exact trace reduction yields a one-dimensional derivative and its unique boundary/interior optimum. All boundary and n=3 multiplicity cases were reconstructed. Standalone exact rational verifier succeeded on 308 checks; the theorem relies on the analytic proof, not finite enumeration.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Renaming the structure as an edge triangulation, triangle expansion or clique with edgewise parallel two-paths does not turn the unweighted Kirchhoff-index formula into an exact optimal priced-conductance allocation. value.rationale: Edge triangulation is a standard graph transform that supplies an alternative two-hop route to every original connection. Under a single budget, selecting which direct edges should carry positive conductance is a natural robustness/resource-allocation question. The result is an exact unrestricted network-design classification: sharp price frontier, all optimal weights and Kirchhoff index, a nontrivial n=8 equal-price support transition, and a 1/n large-order boundary. Its significance is structural, not a small numerical improvement or arbitrary parameter slice.
